info.name: Dhun API
info.description:
Maintained alongside the code. Any endpoint change — added, removed, renamed, new field, new error code — updates this collection in the SAME change. A stale collection is a broken build.

## Conventions

- Every route lives under `/{{apiVersion}}/` (currently v1). Old app versions stay alive forever, so the prefix is never retrofitted.
- Auth is `Bearer {{accessToken}}`, set once at collection level and inherited.
- **Every money endpoint requires an `Idempotency-Key` header** (a UUID). The collection pre-request script generates one automatically for any request whose URL contains `/wallet/`, `/gifts/`, `/cosmetics/` or `/payouts/`.
- `X-Trace-Id` is echoed back on every response and included in every error body. Quote it in bug reports.

## Error envelope

Every failure looks like this:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE", "message": "...", "details": {}, "trace_id": "..." } }
```

Switch on `code`, never on the HTTP status or the message.

## Folder status

Folders map to milestones in `docs/build-plan.md`. Empty ones are not yet built — they are here so the structure is agreed before the endpoints land.

## Errors

Every failure uses the same envelope. Switch on `code`, never on the status or the message.

```json
{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {}, "trace_id": "..." } }
```

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | `details.issues[]` carries `field`, `code`, `message`. Field paths only — your input is never echoed back. |
| `UNSAFE_PAYLOAD` | 400 | Body contained `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` |
| `BAD_JSON` | 400 | Body was not valid JSON |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | Content-Type must be application/json |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Body over 256 KB |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `INVALID_TOKEN` | 401 | Missing or bad bearer token |
| `REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` | 403 | Guest tried to spend — verify a phone first |
| `DOB_REQUIRED` | 403 | **Adult gate.** No date of birth on file. Open the date picker. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Under 18, or missing a role |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Check `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit-*` headers |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` / `_INVALID` | 400 | Money endpoints need a UUID key |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | 422 | Same key, different operation — a client bug |
| `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` | 402 | |
| `SIGNATURE_INVALID` / `RECEIPT_INVALID` | 402 | Payment did not verify |
| `RECEIPT_ALREADY_USED` | 409 | Receipt redeemed by another account |
| `TXN_TYPE_INACTIVE` | 503 | Kill switch is on for that flow |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / `TIMEOUT` | 503 / 504 | Transient — safe to retry |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Always generic. Quote the `trace_id`. |

## Security

- **Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored.** A typo'd key returns 422 rather than being silently dropped.
- **Rate limits** apply per IP, per device and per user. Guest creation is 5/hour per device; money endpoints 30/min per user.
- **Money endpoints require a registered adult.** Authenticated, phone-verified, and 18+ with a date of birth on file.
- 5xx messages are always generic. The detail is in the logs against your `trace_id`.

exec: // Money endpoints must carry an Idempotency-Key. Generating it here means
// it is never forgotten by hand, and re-sending the same request in Postman
// exercises a genuine new operation rather than an accidental replay.
// One trace id per request, echoed back by the server.
// Applies to every request in the collection.

item.name: Health
item.description: Unversioned on purpose — infrastructure probes should not care about API versions.

request.description: Is the process up? Used by the load balancer. Never touches the database.
Can it actually serve? Checks Postgres. Returns 503 when the pool is dead, so a broken instance is pulled from rotation rather than failing user requests.
Proves the error envelope is wired up before any real endpoint exists.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Phone OTP with WhatsApp primary and SMS fallback, JWT access + rotating refresh, guest upgraded in place.

**Run them in order.** Each request saves what the next one needs into the environment, so the whole signup flow works end to end without copying tokens by hand.

`devCode` is returned by the OTP request outside production, which is what makes this runnable before TRAI DLT registration completes.

request.description: Anonymous but real identity, called on first launch. The user can watch, follow and earn free coins before signing up — and keeps all of it, because signup fills in this same row rather than replacing it.
Rate limited to 5 per number per hour. Requesting a new code immediately invalidates the previous one.

exec: // Only present outside production — the console provider logs it there.

request.description:
Sends the guest access token, so the guest is upgraded IN PLACE and keeps its user id. Without a token a brand new registered user is created instead.

If the number already belongs to an account, that account is signed into and the guest row is left alone — balances are never merged between two identities.
Current user with their active scoped role grants.

Sets the profile. **A date of birth is required before any money endpoint will work** — hard rule #5 is enforced where money moves, not just as an optional field, so it cannot be bypassed by skipping the question.

Every session response now carries `user.profileComplete` — display name AND date of birth both set. The client cannot work this out alone because it never sees the date of birth, and without it someone who quit mid-signup came back authenticated and was never asked again.

An under-18 date returns 403 UNDERAGE. Without one, purchases return 403 DOB_REQUIRED so the app knows to open the date picker.

Age is evaluated against the calendar date in IST, so someone turning 18 today passes from 00:00 IST. A date that matches the YYYY-MM-DD shape but is not a real date (`2000-02-31`), or one in the future, returns 422 INVALID_DOB — not UNDERAGE, because a typo must not send a user into an age-appeal flow.

`locale` (`en-IN` | `hi-IN`) is the app's language, so text the server writes — a push notification — matches it. The app sends it whenever the language changes.

Rotates: the presented token is retired and a new pair issued.

Presenting an already-rotated token means two parties hold it, so the entire device chain is revoked and the response is 401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED. Try running this twice in a row to see it.
Revokes refresh tokens for this device, or every device with allDevices: true. The access token stays valid until it expires — that is the trade for stateless auth.

The SECONDARY path. Phone stays primary — it is what India signs up with and what the payout identity is tied to — but an account with no recovery channel is one lost SIM away from an unresolvable ticket.

The account is usable IMMEDIATELY with the address unconfirmed. Blocking signup behind an inbox round trip is where funnels die. What confirmation gates is MONEY: a purchase without a verified phone or email is refused with 403 CONTACT_UNVERIFIED.

Send the guest's Authorization header to UPGRADE that account in place, exactly like phone signup, so nothing earned before signing up is orphaned.

Passwords are scrypt (N=2^17), bounded at 200 characters because a slow hash over an unbounded input is a denial of service costing the attacker one request. 409 EMAIL_TAKEN on a duplicate, matched case-insensitively.

ONE error for every failure — unknown address, wrong password, an account with no password set. Distinguishing them turns the login form into an account-existence oracle, which on an app of this kind can out someone.

A dummy scrypt verification runs when the account does not exist, so the response takes the same ~100ms either way. Without it the TIMING leaks exactly what the shared message hides.

Banned and suspended accounts are refused here as well as on every request.

Sends, or resends, the 6-digit code.

A resend CONSUMES the previous code. Without that, five resends leave five working codes and the attempt limit means five times less than it looks.

5 per address per hour. 409 if the address is already confirmed.

The attempt counter is incremented and COMMITTED before any rejection is thrown — the same trap the OTP flow hit, where the throw rolled back the increment and made brute-force protection theatre.

The code is matched against the address SNAPSHOTTED when it was sent, so a code mailed to an old address cannot confirm a new one.

Only an HMAC of the code is stored: a database dump must not hand over a working confirmation for every pending request.

Exchanges an MSG91 widget access token for a session.

With the widget the app talks to MSG91 DIRECTLY — it sends the code and checks it client-side — so what arrives here is a string the client CLAIMS MSG91 gave it. This route confirms that claim with the account AUTHKEY, which never leaves the server.

Two credentials, two trust levels: the widget's `tokenAuth` ships in the app and is public (a leak costs money), the authkey is server-only (a leak costs accounts).

FAILS CLOSED in every direction — network error, timeout, non-200, unreadable body, a success flag that is not exactly right, or a missing identifier all reject. A provider outage returns 503, not 401, because that is not the user getting it wrong.

An EMAIL identifier is refused on this route: writing one into phone_e164 would break every rule downstream that assumes E.164.

Send the guest's Authorization header to upgrade that account in place.

⚠️ The verification URL is https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/widget/verifyAccessToken. The base path is confirmed from the SDK's own api.url.ts; confirm the leaf against the panel's Server-Side Integration section before going live.

ALWAYS answers 202, whether or not the address exists. Any difference here turns the form into an account-existence oracle.

Only an account that HAS a password is resettable — a phone-only account that happens to carry an email is silently skipped, since resetting it would be a way to add a password to an account you do not control.

The code is emailed. In dev the console provider logs it.

exec: pm.test('says nothing about the account', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ sent: true }));

request.description:
Revokes EVERY refresh token on success. Someone resetting because they were compromised would otherwise leave the attacker signed in — the reset would change the password and nothing else.

Does NOT return a session: sign in again with the new password.

Requires the CURRENT password even though the caller is authenticated: a borrowed unlocked phone must not be able to lock the owner out.

`keepDeviceId` is this device, kept signed in. Every other device is signed out — that is the point of the action. Omit it to sign out everywhere.

query.description: This device, so the response can mark which row not to offer a sign-out on.

request.description: Devices with a LIVE refresh token, this one first. A device with no unrevoked token is not a session and is left out — listing it would make "sign out everywhere" look like it did nothing.
Revokes that device’s refresh tokens. Idempotent — revoking an already-dead session is fine and returns 0.

Sends a code to the NEW number, not the old one. The commonest reason to change is that the old SIM is gone, and a flow that needs the thing you lost is a flow nobody can finish — the password re-proves the account instead, and is REQUIRED whenever the account has one (422 PASSWORD_REQUIRED).

Refuses before sending: 409 PHONE_TAKEN if the number belongs to someone else, 409 PHONE_UNCHANGED if it is already yours. Checking first costs an existence signal on an authenticated, per-user rate-limited endpoint; sending first would let anyone signed in text a stranger on demand.

Guests are refused — signup is the flow they want.

The challenge is stored with purpose `phone_change`, so this code cannot be spent at /auth/otp/verify and a sign-in code cannot be spent here.

Moves the number and returns the updated user.

Every OTHER device is signed out — a number change is a security event whether or not the person meant it as one, and if it was not the owner’s doing, ending the attacker’s session is the only thing that still helps them. `keepDeviceId` is the device making the call.

Written to `phone_changes` and logged at warn: the support ticket after a takeover starts with "when did my number change, and from which device".

The old number is released, so someone else can sign up on it — Indian numbers get recycled.

Required by Google Play for any app with accounts, and by DPDP Act 2023.

ANONYMISES rather than deleting the row: the ledger is append-only and its entries point at this user, so phone, email, password and profile are cleared, the status becomes `deleted`, devices are removed and every session ends. Nulling the address frees it for reuse.

The password is REQUIRED when the account has one (422 PASSWORD_REQUIRED otherwise).

item.name: Catalog
item.description:
Server-driven config. Day-1 non-negotiable #6: adding a gift or changing a price must never need an app release, because old app versions stay alive forever.

Cached 30s in process; an admin edit clears it immediately.

request.description:
20 gifts across 5 tiers, priced for 110 coins/rupee (migration 018 doubled every count).

`payoutRateBp` is PER GIFT, never a global constant, so event gifts can carry a different rate later.

Each gift carries `iconAsset` (every gift) and `animationAsset` (full-screen effects only — NULL for `basic`). Paths are versioned and immutable; until real art lands they sit under `placeholder/`, which production reconciliation refuses. See docs/asset-contract.md.

exec: const gifts = pm.response.json().gifts; if (gifts && gifts.length) pm.environment.set('giftId', gifts[0].id);

request.description:
Priced in GEMS, zero host payout — the margin path. Only the four wearable kinds sell in M7 (frame, chat_bubble, nickname_color, entry_effect); VIP and super message are hidden.

Each item carries `asset` (frame WebP / entry Lottie, null for pure style data) and `style` — validated light/dark style data, see docs/asset-contract.md § 6. An item whose style does not validate is withheld from the catalog rather than sold as a blank.

`conversion` carries the live coins→gems terms (`coinToGemRateBp`, `minimumCoins`) so the store never guesses them.

exec: pm.test('conversion terms travel with the store', () => pm.expect(b.conversion.coinToGemRateBp).to.be.a('number'));

item.name: Wallet
item.description:
Balances, packs, purchases and the coins-to-gems conversion.

**Every endpoint here that moves money requires `Idempotency-Key`** — the collection pre-request script generates one automatically.

For purchases the header is NOT what makes it safe: the ledger key is derived from the receipt, so replaying a captured receipt under a fresh key still credits exactly once. Send request 3 twice with the same `purchaseToken` to see `replayed: true`.

request.description:
Coins, gems, user level, and lifetime purchased coins.

Level accrues on PURCHASE, not on spend — free coins are ordinary coins now, so scoring on spend would let daily check-ins be ground into levels.

The 110 coins/rupee table. Totals match the source doc so advertised value is preserved; only the coin/gem split is new.

Starter is deliberately off-formula (105 coins/rupee) — its job is teaching the gifting loop, not margin.

With `IAP_PROVIDER=stub` a token shaped `stub-xxxxxxxx` is accepted without calling Google, so the whole path works before the Play developer account exists.

The real Google Play verifier is blocked on the M3 spike.

Signature is verified offline: Razorpay signs `order_id|payment_id` with the account key secret, so this path needs no spike and no network call.

The web channel has its own cash account, which is how channel mix becomes a balance read rather than a report.

ONE WAY, +20%. This is the lever that pulls blended payout down: coins pay hosts 30% of face value, gems pay nothing.

There is deliberately no reverse. Gems converting back to coins would let a whale turn cosmetics money into giftable coins and the payout design collapses.
Read from the ledger, joined only on the caller own scoped accounts — a user can never see a system account or another person movements.
Includes status, so a purchase stuck at `pending` (a crash between the receipt and the credit) is visible rather than silent.

item.name: Rooms — M5
item.description:
Room lifecycle and seats. Live chat and presence run over the WebSocket gateway, not REST.

Planned: `GET /v1/rooms`, `POST /v1/rooms`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/join`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/seats/{index}`, `DELETE /v1/rooms/{id}/seats/{index}`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/go-live`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/end`.

request.description:
Live rooms, most watched first. Readable WITHOUT a session — browsing is the top of the funnel and a signed-out user has to see what the app is before being asked for a phone number.

`following` needs a viewer and returns empty without one. `trending` is computed in the same query, so it can never disagree with the ordering.

Starts a broadcast and returns a media token that can SPEAK.

Omit `seatCapacity` for a single-host livestream; include it (2–20) for a party room, where seat 0 is reserved for the host at creation.

Registered users only — a guest may watch and nothing else. A host may have exactly ONE live room: a second attempt returns 409 ALREADY_LIVE carrying the existing roomId rather than replacing it, because a reconnect storm would otherwise churn through rooms and scatter the audience.

Token minting is local, so going live cannot fail because the media server was briefly slow. 503 RTC_UNAVAILABLE means LIVEKIT_* is not configured.
The room and its seat map, without joining. What a feed card expands into.

Returns a media token whose PUBLISH grant comes from the seat table and nowhere else — there is deliberately no way to ask for publish rights in the request.

IMPORTANT: a listener token sets `canPublish: false` EXPLICITLY. LiveKit treats an omitted flag as permission to publish, so a token that merely forgot the field would let any listener talk in any room.

Someone who already holds a seat gets speaking rights back, which is what makes a dropped signal a hiccup rather than losing your place on stage.

403 ROOM_BANNED if the host kicked them; 410 ROOM_ENDED once the room is over.

The primary key on (room_id, seat_index) settles a contested seat — not a read-then-write, which would let two people both be granted the microphone.

On success the media permission is raised to publish. If THAT call fails the seat is released again and a 503 is returned, so nobody is left visibly holding a seat they cannot speak from.

409 SEAT_TAKEN · 403 SEAT_RESERVED (seat 0 belongs to the host) · 422 SEAT_OUT_OF_RANGE · 409 NOT_A_PARTY_ROOM.

One route for two actors: leaving your own seat, or the host removing somebody from theirs. Anyone else gets 403 NOT_ROOM_HOST.

Revoking publish also unpublishes whatever they were sending, so they go quiet rather than merely being unable to start again. The media call is best effort — the seat is already free, and reporting a failure would say the action did not work when it did.

Persisted, because it has to survive the muted person force-quitting the app to escape it — which is exactly what somebody being muted for a reason will do.

NOT best effort, unlike releasing a seat: a mute that never reached the media server has changed nothing anyone can hear, so the row is rolled back and the host is told.

The BAN ROW is what does the work. Disconnecting someone from the media server is cosmetic on its own — their SDK reconnects within seconds — so the row is written first and the disconnect is best effort afterwards.

Room-scoped, and deliberately NOT a platform ban. A host clearing their own room is not a judgement about the account, and letting it become one would hand every host the power to suspend a user.

Our row is closed FIRST, then the media room. If the media call fails the room is already gone from the feed and nobody new can join, and the media server collects the orphan on its empty timeout. The other order would leave a dead card in the feed that users tap repeatedly.

Idempotent — a retry after a dropped response is ordinary. Recorded as `ended_reason = host`, which is what distinguishes it from a broadcast that died (`timeout`) or one a moderator killed.

NOT callable from Postman — the signature is a JWT over a digest of the raw body, signed with LIVEKIT_API_SECRET. Documented here so the endpoint is discoverable.

Mounted BEFORE the JSON body parser: LiveKit signs the RAW BYTES, so a parsed and re-serialised body can never verify, and its `application/webhook+json` content type would be rejected with a 415 first.

Handled: room_started, participant_joined, participant_left, room_finished. Everything else is ignored on purpose — LiveKit adds event types over time and a 500 on one would make it retry forever.

Every handler is safe to run twice and safe to miss: viewer_count is SET from `room.numParticipants` rather than incremented, so a dropped event self-heals on the next one instead of drifting forever.

exec: // Signed by LiveKit. Cannot be exercised by hand.

item.name: Gifting — M6
item.description:
Money endpoint — `Idempotency-Key` required.

The catalog is `GET /v1/catalog/gifts` (Catalog folder). One send is ONE ledger transaction whatever the combo (ledger-decisions § C10), and writes a `gift_sends` row in the same database transaction, which is what the leaderboard reads.

Idempotency identity: `gift_id`, `recipient_id`, `room_id`, `quantity`.

request.description:
Registered, 18+ with a verified contact, `Idempotency-Key` required. Rate limited to 300/min per user — its own scope, because a combo is a thumb tapping several times a second.

`quantity` is one of 1, 10, 99, 520, 999. `expectedCoinPrice` is the unit price the app displayed; a mismatch is refused rather than charged.

The recipient is the host, or anyone on a seat in a party room. On success the gift is published to the room's gateway channel straight after commit (the fast path) and `gift_sent` is written to the outbox (the durable one).

A retry with the same key returns the original gift with `replayed: true` — even if the room has ended since.

**Errors:** `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` 402 · `GIFT_TO_SELF` 422 · `GIFT_PRICE_CHANGED` 409 (details.coinPrice) · `GIFT_NOT_FOUND` 404 · `RECIPIENT_NOT_IN_ROOM` 409 (also returned when the recipient has blocked the sender, deliberately indistinguishable) · `ROOM_NOT_FOUND` 404 · `ROOM_ENDED` 410 · `ROOM_BANNED` 403 · `TXN_TYPE_INACTIVE` 503 (kill switch) · `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` 422 · `REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` 409 · `REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` / `DOB_REQUIRED` / `CONTACT_UNVERIFIED` 403.

exec: pm.test('one transaction for the whole combo', () => {
pm.test('the gift id is the ledger transaction', () => pm.expect(b.gift.id).to.be.a('string'));

request.description:
Top 20 senders in the room by total coins given. Readable without a session, like the room itself. Read from `gift_sends`, written in the same transaction as the money, so it can never disagree with the ledger. Ties go to whoever reached the total first.

An empty list is a real room with no gifts; an unknown room is `ROOM_NOT_FOUND` 404.

exec: for (let i = 1; i < board.length; i++) pm.expect(board[i - 1].coins).to.be.at.least(board[i].coins);

item.name: Cosmetics — M7
item.description:
Buying, owning and wearing cosmetics. Purchases are money endpoints — registered, 18+, `Idempotency-Key` required.

Ownership rules (ledger-decisions § C11c/C11d): every purchase is one full-price transaction; time is ADDED to the current expiry while an item is active and restarts from now once it has lapsed; buying equips; one equipped item per kind; expiry is evaluated on read and nothing is swept.

Worn items appear as `look` on room seats, chat lines, gift senders (`senderFrame`), public profiles and the owner's summary. Someone wearing an entry effect is announced to a room over the gateway (`t: 'entry'`), at most once per room per 5 minutes.

request.description: Everything the caller holds, newest expiry first. Lapsed items stay listed with `active: false` so they can be renewed; an expired item is never reported as equipped.

Spends gems only — never coins, whatever the coin balance. `expectedGemPrice` is the price the store displayed; a repriced item is refused, not charged. A retry with the same key replays the original purchase, even after a reprice; a key reused for another item or by another account is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

**Errors:** `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` 402 · `COSMETIC_PRICE_CHANGED` 409 (details.gemPrice) · `COSMETIC_NOT_FOUND` 404 (also VIP and super message, not sold in M7) · `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` 422 · `REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` 409 · `TXN_TYPE_INACTIVE` 503 · `REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` / `DOB_REQUIRED` / `CONTACT_UNVERIFIED` 403.

Wears an owned, active item and takes off whatever else of its kind was worn. Moves no money, so no Idempotency-Key.

**Errors:** `COSMETIC_NOT_OWNED` 404 · `COSMETIC_EXPIRED` 410.
Takes off whatever of this kind is worn. `kind` is one of frame, chat_bubble, nickname_color, entry_effect. Taking off nothing is not an error.

item.name: Host & Payouts — M8
item.description:
Verification and withdrawals. Maker-checker is enforced by the system, not by policy — one person can never both prepare and approve.

Planned: `POST /v1/host/apply`, `POST /v1/host/verify/pan`, `POST /v1/host/verify/bank`, `POST /v1/host/verify/face`, `GET /v1/host/earnings`, `POST /v1/payouts/request`, `GET /v1/payouts`.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Ships with every milestone rather than as a phase of its own — the docs are explicit that the admin panel is part of the MVP.

Planned: catalog editing (M4), room monitoring (M5), payout approval (M8), moderator dashboard (M9), and transaction-type kill switches (`PATCH /v1/admin/txn-types/{code}` — flipping `is_active` stops a money flow platform-wide with no deploy).

request.description:
The feed the app opens on. **No session required** — browsing is the top of the funnel and a signed-out user must see what the app is before being asked for a phone number.

`category=explore` returns single-host rooms, `party` returns rooms with seats, `following` needs a session and returns EMPTY without one rather than silently ignoring the filter.

Ended rooms never appear. `trending` marks the top ten by viewers and is computed in the same query, so it can never disagree with the order.

Private by definition — 401 without a session.

Unread is counted from the participant's read WATERMARK, not a stored counter: a counter has to be decremented correctly from several places and drifts the first time one is missed.

`filter` is one of all | official | unread | groups.

Everything the Me screen shows that is not a balance: follower counts, unseen profile visitors, level, and the withdrawable points balance.

`friends` is a follow in BOTH directions, computed rather than stored so it can never disagree with the follow rows.

`verified` means PHONE verified, which is what gates money endpoints today. The payout KYC badge — PAN plus face match, hard rule #5 — is a stricter, separate check that arrives with payouts in M8.

`publicId` is the short number a user reads out to be found. Never the internal uuid.

The campaign strip above the feed. Server-driven from day one (non-negotiable #6): a campaign must never need an app release, and a bad banner is killed in seconds by flipping `is_active`.

Expired banners are filtered by the query, not by a sweep — a banner whose countdown has run out is worse than no banner.

⚠️ HARD RULE #1: `action` is a CLOSED set (ranking | rewards | topup | none). An event may be a ranking; it may never be chance. No lucky box, no wheel, no mystery gift.

IDEMPOTENT — following twice is a no-op, not a 409. A double tap on a slow connection is the common case, and an error there would be shown to a user who did exactly the right thing.

Allowed for a GUEST: a guest is a real server-side identity, and following is the retention loop that gives them a reason to come back. Rate-limited to 200/hour per USER — far above any human, far below a script building a graph.

422 CANNOT_FOLLOW_SELF, 404 USER_NOT_FOUND.
Also idempotent. Unfollowing someone you never followed is not an error.
Who looked at your profile, newest first, each with whether you already follow them — so the button renders correctly without a second call.

Clears the "N new" badge and returns how many were cleared.

POST rather than GET because it CHANGES STATE: a GET that mutates gets fired by a prefetcher and clears a badge nobody looked at.

Upserted, not appended — the question is "who has been looking", not "how many times", and append-only grows without bound for a popular host.

Re-visiting refreshes the timestamp AND clears seen_at, so a returning visitor surfaces again.

Visiting your own profile is silently ignored: the client cannot always know whose profile it is opening. 204 No Content.
Membership is checked in the WHERE clause, not by a separate lookup — one query that returns nothing for a non-member cannot be raced by a membership change between the check and the read.

Moves the read WATERMARK to now. Idempotent, so it is safe on every open, and still correct after a message is deleted — which a counter is not.

404 for a thread you are not in, NOT 403: telling a stranger that a thread exists but is not theirs is itself a leak.

Force-update floor and remote feature flags — day-1 non-negotiable #5.

ANONYMOUS on purpose: a force-update has to reach a user who cannot sign in, which is exactly the situation a broken auth release creates.

Flags here are the NON-money switches. The money layer has a stronger one — ledger_txn_types.is_active stops a flow inside the transaction — so a client that ignores a flag, or a modified build that never asks, still cannot move coins.

Non-boolean flag values are dropped rather than passed through.

What a STRANGER may see — deliberately narrower than your own summary: no points balance, no unseen-visitor count, no date of birth, no phone. Deciding what a stranger sees is a trust-and-safety question, so a field is absent until someone decides it should be there.

Returns 404 when either party has blocked the other, and for a banned account. NOT 403 — a 403 confirms the account exists.

Store review REQUIRES a working report mechanism for user-generated content. This is the intake half; queue triage, strikes and appeals are M9.

`reason` is a CLOSED set mapped to the policy levels in trust-and-safety-v1 — free text alone cannot be triaged, counted, or turned into a threshold that pages someone.

One row per reporter per subject per day. Twenty people reporting the same host is the strongest signal moderation has; one person reporting twenty times is not. A same-day repeat returns `filed: false` and still 202, because telling a user off for reporting teaches them not to.

202 Accepted, not 201: the report is recorded, and whether it results in anything is a human decision later.

Takes effect immediately and in BOTH directions — neither party sees the other's rooms in any feed. A one-way block that leaves the blocked person able to watch is a mute, not a block.

Does NOT unfollow: blocking and unfollowing are separate intentions, and a user who blocks then unblocks should not silently lose a follow they chose.

This is the remedy a user can apply without waiting for a moderator, which matters because the gap between reporting and review is hours at best.
Idempotent.

item.name: Rewards — M10
item.description:
Free coins: ordinary coins, giftable at the full payout rate (CLAUDE.md supersedes the 20%/expiring bonus design). Amounts and caps are `app_config.free_coins`. No Idempotency-Key header: the ledger key is DERIVED FROM THE CLAIM (`checkin:{user}:{IST date}` …), so repeating a claim can never pay twice. Registered accounts only. Kill switch: `ledger_txn_types.free_coin_grant`. Decisions: ledger-decisions § C5b, C5c.

The watch reward has no endpoint — the realtime gateway measures time in a room and pays it, pushing `{t:'reward'}` to the watcher.

request.description: Welcome bonus (claimed / available — unavailable when another account on the same phone took it), today's check-in (ladder, claimedToday, streakDay), watch progress, and referral stats with the caller's invite code (their public ID).

500 coins, once per account and once per device. A repeat returns `alreadyClaimed: true`.

**Errors:** `WELCOME_ALREADY_USED_ON_DEVICE` 409 · `REWARD_UNAVAILABLE` 409 · `TXN_TYPE_INACTIVE` 503 · `REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` 403.
Ladder 20, 30, 40, 60, 80, 100, 150 on consecutive IST days, wrapping after day 7; a missed day resets to day 1. One claim per IST day — a repeat returns `alreadyClaimed: true`.

The referrer's public ID. Within 7 days of signup, once, never your own, never from an account on the same phone. The referrer is paid 2,000 coins when this account's first purchase of at least ₹99 is credited — by the workers' outbox consumer, not here.

**Errors:** `REFERRAL_CODE_INVALID` 404 · `REFERRAL_SELF` 422 · `REFERRAL_NOT_ALLOWED` 422 · `REFERRAL_ALREADY_SET` 409 · `REFERRAL_WINDOW_CLOSED` 409.

item.name: Discover — M10
item.description: Search and the cold-start helpers. Readable without a session.

request.description: People by name PREFIX (case-insensitive) or exact public ID; live rooms by title or host name. Blocks hide in both directions. People carry `look` and `liveRoomId`. Viewer counts are null while cold start hides them.
Where a brand-new user is dropped on first open (growth-plan-v1). Never the caller's own room, never across a block. `room: null` when nothing is live or `cold_start.dropNewUsersIntoRoom` is off.

item.name: Notifications — M10
item.description: Expo push tokens. The followed-host-is-live push is sent by the workers when `room_started` is consumed: once per follower per room, once per host per cooldown, a daily cap per person, never across a block, never for a room that has already ended. A token registered by a new account is removed from any other account holding it. Copy is written server-side in the follower's `locale`.

request.description: For the device this session signed in on. **Errors:** `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` 404 · `VALIDATION_FAILED` 422 (not an Expo token).
